text: Does the rash also appear in the diaper area or behind the ears, and does it seem to worsen when the skin gets dry or irritated? I also need to know if there is any family history of eczema or asthma on the mother's side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the greasy yellow scales and location on the scalp and forehead in an infant, this presentation is classic for seborrheic dermatitis, often referred to as "cradle cap." speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead in a 3-month-old infant is highly characteristic of seborrheic dermatitis, commonly known as cradle cap. While the family history of psoriasis is noted, the age and specific morphology strongly favor a benign, self-limiting condition rather than infantile psoriasis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic dermatitis
